# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL v2.1 | PAGE 1 OF 11

## A

Climate change, particularly by single and industrial agriculture, is a significant driver of climate change. Agriculture contributes to greenhouse gas emissions through land use changes, livestock production, and fertilizer use. The Green Climate Fund (GCF) seeks to support and strengthen the capacity of developing countries to adapt to climate change and mitigate its impacts.

The impact of climate change on agriculture and farming systems is projected to mount in several ways. By 2050, it is estimated that global crop yields could fall by up to 15% due to climate change-related losses by 2030, and an even greater loss by 2080. Climate change will also affect the availability of water resources for irrigation, which are critical for agriculture.

The project's objective is to address these challenges through improved land management practices in Kenya's Eastern Province. This initiative aims to build resilience to climate change and improve food security in the region. The project will focus on sustainable land management practices that enhance soil fertility, increase crop yields, and reduce greenhouse gas emissions.

### Outcomes

1. A shift to farming practices that build resilience against climate threats and risks.
2. Strengthened adaptive capacity and reduced exposure to climate risks.
3. Improved access to finance for smallholder farmers to implement adaptation measures.

- **Outcome 3:** Improved access to finance for smallholder farmers to implement adaptation measures.

## Component 1: Mobilize and valorize climate development for climate-resilient agricultural land use products linked to agroforestry systems

This component will promote the adoption of agroforestry systems and sustainable land management practices. It will also support the development of financial instruments to facilitate access to credit by smallholder farmers. The project will provide technical assistance to farmers to improve their productivity and resilience to climate change. It will also support the development of market linkages for climate-resilient agricultural products.

### Sub-component 1.1: Agroforestry systems

This sub-component will promote the adoption of agroforestry systems by smallholder farmers. It will provide technical assistance to farmers to establish and manage agroforestry systems. It will also support the development of market linkages for agroforestry products.

### Sub-component 1.2: Sustainable land management practices

This sub-component will promote the adoption of sustainable land management practices by smallholder farmers. It will provide technical assistance to farmers to improve their productivity and resilience to climate change. It will also support the development of market linkages for climate-resilient agricultural products.

## Component 2: Strengthened enabling environment to effectively plan, manage and monitor climate adaptation investments

This component will promote the development of a comprehensive framework for climate adaptation planning and implementation. It will also support the establishment of a national climate adaptation fund to finance climate adaptation projects. The project will provide technical assistance to government agencies to improve their capacity to plan, manage and monitor climate adaptation investments.

### Sub-component 2.1: National climate adaptation planning

This sub-component will promote the development of a comprehensive framework for climate adaptation planning. It will provide technical assistance to government agencies to improve their capacity to plan for climate change. It will also support the establishment of a national climate adaptation fund to finance climate adaptation projects.

### Sub-component 2.2: National climate adaptation fund

This sub-component will promote the establishment of a national climate adaptation fund to finance climate adaptation projects. It will provide technical assistance to government agencies to improve their capacity to manage and monitor climate adaptation investments.

The objective of this project is to provide a comprehensive assessment of the economic and ecosystem costs associated with the loss of natural capital in the Eastern Province. In 2018, the agricultural sector accounted for more than 35% of GDP and 87% of the population is engaged in agriculture. Submitted all 10 million metric tons per year which is equivalent to saving the entirety of the forest and to feed 65 million people annually. The project will be implemented in the Eastern Province, specifically in the districts of Bugesera, Kirehe, Rwamagana, Kayonza, Ngoma, and Rutsiro. The project will contribute to achieving the objectives of the National Strategy for Transformation (NST1), which aims to promote sustainable development, family and group-based farming, and climate change resilience. Additionally, it will contribute to the country's commitment to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 38% by 2030.

The project will be implemented in two phases: Phase I involves the preparation of a detailed feasibility study and environmental impact assessment (EIA). Phase II includes the actual implementation of the project. The project will be carried out over a period of five years, with an estimated cost of $15 million.

# Green Climate Fund Funding Proposal

## Project Title: Integrated Landscape Approach to Enhance Resilience and Increase Agricultural Productivity in Eastern Province

### Project Description
The project aims to enhance climate resilience and increase agricultural productivity in the Eastern Province of Kenya. It focuses on improving water management, soil health, and crop diversification.

### Objectives
- **Objective 1:** Improve water management practices.
- **Objective 2:** Enhance soil fertility and conservation.
- **Objective 3:** Promote climate-smart agriculture.

### Project Location
Eastern Province, Kenya

### Project Duration
January 2014 - December 2018

### Total Budget
USD 5,000,000

### Funding Requested
USD 4,000,000 (80% of total budget)

### Co-Financing
USD 1,000,000 (20% from national and local governments)

## Historical Climate Trends in the Eastern Province
The Eastern Province has experienced significant changes in climate patterns over recent decades. These include:

- **Rainfall:** Decreased rainfall intensity and increased frequency of droughts.
- **Temperature:** Higher temperatures, prolonged dry periods, and second-time evapotranspiration have resulted in reduced soil moisture.

### Impacts on Agriculture
In the past five decades, rainfall/reduced has been affected by climate-induced droughts, leading to:

- Reduced crop yields.
- Increased incidence of pests and diseases.

- **Soil Health:** Promote sustainable land management practices.

- Improved water management practices.
- Enhanced soil fertility and conservation.
- Increased agricultural productivity and resilience to climate change.

### Areas of Focus

- **Agriculture:** Enhancing the role of farming in more climate-resilient food systems.
- **Forestry:** Improving forest and soil carbon stocks.
- **Industrial Processes:** Reducing emissions from industrial processes.

### Key Objectives

- **Climate Resilience:** Enhance climate resilience through improved land use, water management, and sustainable agriculture.
- **Emissions Reduction:** Reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions by 30% by 2030 compared to business-as-usual scenarios.
- **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs):** Align with SDGs to ensure climate action supports broader development goals.

### Funding Strategy

- **Green Climate Fund (GCF):** Leverage GCF resources for climate adaptation and mitigation projects.
- **Public and Private Sector:** Engage both public and private sectors in financing climate initiatives.
- **International Cooperation:** Collaborate with international organizations, such as the World Bank and IMF, to enhance funding efforts.

### Project Examples

#### Renewable Energy Projects

- **Solar Power:** Transition from fossil fuels to renewable energy sources like solar power.
- **Wind Energy:** Develop wind farms for sustainable electricity generation.

#### Climate Adaptation Initiatives

- **Water Management:** Implement water management strategies to mitigate climate change impacts.
- **Disaster Resilience:** Enhance disaster resilience through improved infrastructure and early warning systems.

### Existing Climate Change Adaptation Interventions

- **National Adaptation Programs of Action (NAPAs):** Identify priority actions for adaptation in vulnerable sectors.
- **Climate-Smart Agriculture:** Promote climate-smart agriculture practices to enhance food security.

### Key Projects

#### Renewable Energy Sector - Rwanda (RENEW)

- **Objective:** Transition to renewable energy sources.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding mechanisms.
- **Implementation:** Collaboration with local governments and communities.

#### Forest Management and Domestic Energy Project - Tanzania (FORESTMAN)

- **Objective:** Improve forest management and reduce reliance on traditional biomass for domestic energy.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding sources.
- **Implementation:** Community-based approaches to forest conservation and sustainable energy use.

#### Northern Basin (NPST2) - FORESTER

- **Objective:** Enhance forest resilience and carbon sequestration in the Northern Basin.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding mechanisms.
- **Implementation:** Collaboration with local communities and stakeholders.

### Land Husbandry, Water Harvesting, and Mitigation Project - World Bank and MNNAGE

- **Objective:** Improve land management practices to enhance water harvesting and mitigate climate change impacts.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding sources.
- **Implementation:** Community-based approaches to sustainable land use.

### Runoff Sponge Supper Program (RSSP) - World Bank and MNNAGE

- **Objective:** Enhance water retention in landscapes through runoff sponge technologies.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding mechanisms.
- **Implementation:** Collaboration with local communities and stakeholders.

### Climate Resilience Initiatives in Gambia, Senegal, and the Sahel Region

- **Objective:** Enhance climate resilience in vulnerable regions.
- **Funding:** GCF and other international funding sources.
- **Implementation:** Community-based approaches to sustainable development.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL

## B

### Adaptation measures

The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is designed to address climate change impacts. There is an element of future climate impacts with and beyond the GCF funding. This Bill may require the Government to consider the implications as well as capturing the benefits of adaptation investments. The GCF Board has approved a number of projects that will help countries adapt to climate change. These include:

- **Early Warning Systems**: Helping communities prepare for extreme weather events.
- **Resilient Infrastructure**: Building infrastructure that can withstand climate impacts.
- **Climate-Smart Agriculture**: Supporting farmers to adapt their practices.

### Disaster Risk Management

Disaster risk management is a key component of adaptation. The GCF has funded projects that help countries manage disaster risks, including:

- **Early Warning Systems**: Providing timely and accurate information about impending disasters.
- **Resilient Infrastructure**: Building infrastructure that can withstand natural hazards.
- **Community-Based Disaster Risk Management (CBDRM)**: Empowering communities to prepare for and respond to disasters.

### Knowledge Sharing

The GCF encourages knowledge sharing among countries. This includes:

- **South-South Cooperation**: Exchange of experiences, best practices, and technologies between developing countries.
- **Capacity Building**: Training and education to enhance the skills and capabilities of those working on climate change adaptation.

### Technical / scientific barriers

Technological and scientific barriers can hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Research and Development**: Supporting research into new technologies and methods for adaptation.
- **Knowledge Management**: Sharing knowledge and best practices among countries.
- **Capacity Building**: Enhancing the skills and capabilities of those working on adaptation.

### Financial Barriers

Financial barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Funding Adaptation Projects**: Providing funding for projects that help countries adapt to climate change.
- **Mobilizing Private Sector Finance**: Encouraging private sector investment in adaptation projects.
- **Blending Finance**: Combining public and private funds to support adaptation projects.

### Policy Barriers

Policy barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Policy Reform**: Helping countries reform their policies to better support adaptation.
- **Building Capacity for Policy Making**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to develop and implement effective policies.
- **Promoting Multi-Stakeholder Engagement**: Encouraging engagement between governments, private sector, and civil society in policy making.

### Institutional Barriers

Institutional barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Strengthening Institutions**: Helping countries strengthen their institutions for effective adaptation.
- **Building Capacity for Implementation**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to implement adaptation projects.
- **Promoting Multi-Stakeholder Engagement**: Encouraging engagement between governments, private sector, and civil society in implementation.

### Social Barriers

Social barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Community-Based Adaptation**: Helping communities adapt to climate change.
- **Promoting Gender Equality**: Ensuring that adaptation projects are inclusive and equitable.
- **Building Capacity for Social Inclusion**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to include marginalized groups in adaptation projects.

### Economic Barriers

Economic barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Economic Diversification**: Helping countries diversify their economies to reduce vulnerability to climate change.
- **Promoting Green Economy**: Supporting the transition to a green economy that is resilient to climate change.
- **Building Capacity for Economic Planning**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to plan and implement economic policies that support adaptation.

### Legal Barriers

Legal barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Legal Reform**: Helping countries reform their laws to better support adaptation.
- **Building Capacity for Legal Implementation**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to implement legal frameworks for adaptation.
- **Promoting Multi-Stakeholder Engagement**: Encouraging engagement between governments, private sector, and civil society in legal implementation.

### Political Barriers

Political barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Political Dialogue**: Facilitating dialogue among countries to build consensus on adaptation.
- **Promoting Multi-Stakeholder Engagement**: Encouraging engagement between governments, private sector, and civil society in political processes.
- **Building Capacity for Political Leadership**: Enhancing the capacity of leaders to champion effective adaptation.

### Cultural Barriers

Cultural barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Cultural Preservation**: Helping countries preserve their cultural heritage while adapting to climate change.
- **Promoting Cultural Exchange**: Facilitating exchange of cultural practices and knowledge among countries.
- **Building Capacity for Cultural Sensitivity**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to be sensitive to cultural differences in adaptation projects.

### Technological Barriers

Technological barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Research and Development**: Funding research into new technologies for adaptation.
- **Promoting Technology Transfer**: Facilitating the transfer of technology among countries.
- **Building Capacity for Technology Use**: Enhancing the capacity of governments to use new technologies for adaptation.

### Environmental Barriers

Environmental barriers can also hinder effective adaptation. The GCF aims to overcome these barriers by:

- **Supporting Ecosystem Restoration**: Helping countries restore their ecosystems to enhance resilience to climate change.
- **Promoting Biodiversity Conservation**: Supporting efforts to conserve biodiversity in the face of climate change.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL v2.0 | PAGE 21 OF 119

## B

The GCF is designed to support both mitigation and adaptation projects in developing countries.

### (a) Funding for mitigation

Funding for mitigation is expected to cover approved schedules and activities that reduce greenhouse gas emissions by at least 20% compared to business-as-usual scenarios. This includes:

- Renewable energy projects
- Energy efficiency improvements
- Sustainable transport initiatives
- Forest conservation and reforestation programs

### (b) Funding for adaptation

Funding for adaptation is intended to support projects that build resilience and reduce vulnerability to the adverse effects of climate change. This includes:

- Water management systems
- Early warning systems
- Climate-resilient infrastructure
- Disaster risk reduction strategies
- Agricultural practices that enhance food security

### (c) Funding for cross-cutting issues

Funding for cross-cutting issues aims to address gender equality, social inclusion, and environmental safeguards. This includes:

- Gender-responsive programming
- Social inclusion activities
- Environmental and social impact assessments
- Community engagement and participation

### (d) Funding for knowledge sharing and capacity building

Funding for knowledge sharing and capacity building supports the development of human capital and institutional capacities in developing countries. This includes:

- Training programs and workshops
- Research and development initiatives
- Knowledge management systems
- Technical assistance and advisory services

### (e) Funding for private sector engagement

Funding for private sector engagement aims to leverage private sector investments and expertise to achieve climate objectives. This includes:

- Public-private partnerships
- Blended finance arrangements
- Private sector investment facilitation
- Policy dialogue and regulatory frameworks

### (f) Funding for monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV)

Funding for MRV supports the tracking of project progress and the measurement of greenhouse gas emissions reductions. This includes:

- Development of MRV systems
- Data collection and analysis
- Reporting on project outcomes
- Verification of emission reductions

### (g) Funding for administrative costs

Funding for administrative costs covers the operational expenses of the GCF Secretariat and accredited entities. This includes:

- Staff salaries and benefits
- Office expenses
- Travel and accommodation costs
- Equipment and technology purchases

### (h) Funding for project preparation and planning

Funding for project preparation and planning supports the development of bankable projects that are ready for implementation. This includes:

- Feasibility studies
- Environmental and social impact assessments
- Project design and engineering
- Financial structuring and resource mobilization

### (i) Funding for risk management

Funding for risk management aims to mitigate potential risks associated with project implementation. This includes:

- Insurance coverage
- Contingency funds
- Risk assessment and mitigation strategies
- Crisis response and recovery planning

### (j) Funding for innovation and demonstration projects

Funding for innovation and demonstration projects supports the development of new technologies and approaches that can be scaled up in the future. This includes:

- Pilot projects
- Proof-of-concept studies
- Technology transfer initiatives
- Knowledge sharing and dissemination activities

### (k) Funding for regional and thematic programs

Funding for regional and thematic programs aims to support coordinated efforts across regions and sectors. This includes:

- Regional cooperation initiatives
- Thematic programs addressing cross-cutting issues
- Multi-country projects
- Regional knowledge sharing and capacity building

### (l) Funding for monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL)

Funding for MEL supports the assessment of project outcomes and impacts, as well as the continuous improvement of GCF-funded activities. This includes:

- Development of MEL frameworks
- Data collection and analysis
- Reporting on project performance
- Learning events and knowledge sharing

### (m) Funding for communication and outreach

Funding for communication and outreach aims to raise awareness and promote the achievements of GCF-funded projects. This includes:

- Public relations campaigns
- Media outreach activities
- Stakeholder engagement initiatives
- Event organization and participation

### (n) Funding for legal and regulatory frameworks

Funding for legal and regulatory frameworks supports the development of policies, laws, and regulations that enable climate action. This includes:

- Policy formulation and analysis
- Legal and regulatory framework development
- Institutional strengthening
- Policy dialogue and advocacy

### (o) Funding for capacity building in developing countries

Funding for capacity building in developing countries aims to enhance the skills and capabilities of individuals and institutions in developing countries. This includes:

- Training programs and workshops
- Research and development initiatives
- Knowledge management systems
- Technical assistance and advisory services

### (p) Funding for climate finance tracking and reporting

Funding for climate finance tracking and reporting supports the monitoring and reporting of climate finance flows. This includes:

- Development of tracking systems
- Data collection and analysis
- Reporting on climate finance commitments
- Public disclosure and transparency initiatives

### (q) Funding for climate change education and awareness

Funding for climate change education and awareness aims to increase public understanding and engagement with climate change issues. This includes:

- Educational programs and materials
- Awareness-raising campaigns
- Community outreach activities
- Public events and forums

### (r) Funding for climate change research and development

Funding for climate change research and development supports the generation of new knowledge and technologies to address climate change. This includes:

- Research projects and studies
- Development of new technologies and approaches
- Knowledge sharing and dissemination activities
- Collaboration with academic and research institutions

### (s) Funding for climate change policy and planning

Funding for climate change policy and planning supports the development of national and regional climate change policies and strategies. This includes:

- Policy formulation and analysis
- Strategic planning and implementation
- Institutional strengthening
- Policy dialogue and advocacy

## B

### Introduction

The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is a financial mechanism under the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC). The GCF was established to support developing countries in their efforts to address climate change and its impacts. This document outlines the proposal for a Theory of Change (ToC) that aims to guide the implementation of the project.

### Theory of Change

The ToC is designed to address the identified barriers to adaptation, focusing on the Theory of Change (ToC). The project will be based on a robust Theory of Change that identifies the key elements required to achieve the desired outcomes. This includes the following:

- **Outcome 1:** A shift in farming practices that build resilience against climate threats and risks.
- **Outcome 2:** Strengthened institutional and regulatory systems for climate-responsive planning and development.
- **Outcome 3:** Enhanced capacity of local governments, communities, and other stakeholders to implement adaptation measures.

### Objectives

The project aims to achieve the following objectives:

1. **Objective 1:** Develop and strengthen farming competencies and produce goods and services that are resilient to climate change.
2. **Objective 2:** Strengthen institutional capacities at national, regional, and local levels for climate-responsive planning and development.
3. **Objective 3:** Enhance the capacity of local governments, communities, and other stakeholders to implement adaptation measures.

### Activities

To achieve these objectives, the project will include the following activities:

1. **Activity 1:** Develop and strengthen farming competencies and produce goods and services that are resilient to climate change.
2. **Activity 2:** Strengthen institutional capacities at national, regional, and local levels for climate-responsive planning and development.
3. **Activity 3:** Enhance the capacity of local governments, communities, and other stakeholders to implement adaptation measures.

### Implementation

The project will be implemented over a period of five years, with the following milestones:

- **Year 1:** Conduct baseline studies and develop the project plan.
- **Years 2-4:** Implement activities and monitor progress.
- **Year 5:** Evaluate outcomes and document lessons learned.

### Monitoring and Evaluation

The project will include a comprehensive monitoring and evaluation (M&E) system to track progress towards the objectives. This will include regular reporting on outputs, outcomes, and impacts.

### Conclusion

This proposal outlines the Theory of Change for a project aimed at enhancing climate resilience in developing countries. The project aims to achieve three main objectives through a series of activities implemented over five years.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL

The water management and healthy wetland are major areas where support through TREPA's underwritten emission reduction project can be applied. The project is designed to improve water quality, which is presented by climate change and water management issues. Besides, the project will also address the issue of biodiversity loss and ecosystem degradation. The project will focus on the restoration of degraded wetlands as a major solution to achieve the objectives.

## 2.1 Projecting

### 2.1.1 Description

The project aims to restore and manage 50 hectares of degraded wetlands in Eastern Province from September 2019 to September 2024. The project will be implemented through a combination of activities such as wetland restoration, biodiversity conservation, and community engagement.

### 2.1.2 Objectives

- Restore and maintain the ecological functions of the wetlands.
- Improve water quality and reduce sediment runoff into Lake Victoria.
- Enhance biodiversity by restoring native plant and animal species.
- Increase community awareness and participation in wetland management.

## 2.2 Project Components

### Component 1: Wetland Restoration

This component will focus on restoring the ecological functions of the wetlands through activities such as planting native vegetation, removing invasive species, and improving water flow.

### Component 2: Biodiversity Conservation

This component will focus on enhancing biodiversity by reintroducing native plant and animal species, creating habitats for wildlife, and monitoring biodiversity.

### Component 3: Community Engagement

This component will focus on engaging the local community in wetland management through education, awareness-raising, and participatory decision-making processes.

## 2.3 Project Implementation Strategy

The project will be implemented through a gender transformative approach that is inclusive and adds value to climate change adaptation and resilience-building efforts. The project design is guided by the principles of gender equality and social inclusion, ensuring that women and marginalized groups are actively involved in decision-making processes and benefit equally from the project.

## 2.4 Project Management

The project will be implemented by the National Wetland Conservation Agency (NWCA) with technical support from the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP). The project will be monitored and evaluated by an independent third-party auditor to ensure that it meets its objectives and delivers results in a timely and cost-effective manner.

## 2.5 Project Budget

The total budget for the project is $1,000,000, with $800,000 allocated to wetland restoration activities, $150,000 to biodiversity conservation activities, and $50,000 to community engagement activities.

## 2.6 Project Timeline

The project will be implemented over a period of five years, from September 2019 to September 2024. The project will be divided into three phases: the preparatory phase (September 2019 - December 2019), the implementation phase (January 2020 - December 2023), and the closure phase (January 2024 - September 2024).

## 2.7 Project Risks

The project faces several risks, including:

- Climate change-related risks such as changes in precipitation patterns and increased frequency of extreme weather events.
- Technical risks related to the implementation of wetland restoration activities.
- Financial risks related to the availability of funding for the project.

These risks will be managed through a comprehensive risk management plan that includes contingency measures and regular monitoring and evaluation of project progress.

## 2.8 Project Monitoring and Evaluation

The project will be monitored and evaluated using a results-based approach, with clear indicators and targets for each component. The monitoring and evaluation system will include regular reporting, site visits, and stakeholder consultations to ensure that the project is on track to achieve its objectives.

## Section B

### Objective 2.3 Enhanced Financial Incentives and Investments in Climate-Smart Value Chains (EIE)

- **2.3.1** Enhance financial incentives for climate-smart value chains.
- **2.3.2** Promote investments in climate-smart value chains.
- **2.3.3** Facilitate access to finance and investment opportunities.

#### 2.3.1 Enhanced Financial Incentives

- Provide financial incentives to farmers, cooperatives, and other actors in the value chain for adopting climate-smart practices.
- Encourage investments by providing risk mitigation instruments such as insurance products.
- Promote public-private partnerships (PPPs) to leverage private sector investments.

#### 2.3.2 Promote Investments

- Facilitate access to finance through innovative financial instruments and blended financing mechanisms.
- Support the development of climate-smart value chains by providing technical assistance and capacity building.
- Encourage investments in climate-smart agriculture by offering incentives such as tax breaks, grants, and low-interest loans.

#### 2.3.3 Facilitate Access to Finance

- Develop innovative financial products tailored to the needs of smallholder farmers, cooperatives, and other actors in the value chain.
- Promote access to finance through partnerships with financial institutions, development banks, and microfinance providers.
- Encourage investments by providing guarantees, insurance products, and other risk mitigation instruments.

### Additional Measures

- **2.3.4** Facilitate access to climate-smart technologies for smallholder farmers.
  - Promote the adoption of climate-smart technologies through awareness campaigns and training programs.
  - Provide financial incentives for the purchase and use of climate-smart technologies.
  - Support research and development efforts to improve the accessibility and affordability of climate-smart technologies.

- **2.3.5** Enhance capacity building and knowledge management.
  - Develop and implement training programs for farmers, cooperatives, and other actors in the value chain.
  - Establish information centers and help desks to provide technical assistance and advisory services.
  - Promote knowledge sharing and best practices through networks and partnerships.

### Implementation

- **2.3.6** Strengthen institutional capacity.
  - Provide training and capacity building for government officials, extension workers, and other stakeholders.
  - Establish partnerships with international organizations, development agencies, and private sector entities to enhance technical expertise and resources.
  - Develop policies and regulations that support the implementation of climate-smart value chains.

- **2.3.7** Monitor and evaluate progress.
  - Establish indicators and metrics to track the performance of climate-smart value chains.
  - Conduct regular assessments and evaluations to identify challenges and opportunities for improvement.
  - Publish reports and case studies to share lessons learned and best practices.

### Conclusion

# GREEN CLIMATE FUNDING PROPOSAL

## Chapter 1.2: Support Climate-Smart Agriculture and Forestry

### Objective

Support climate-smart agriculture and forestry to enhance knowledge and practices for adaptation and mitigation of climate change and improve food security.

### Key Results

- **Objective 1.2.1:** Enhance knowledge on climate-smart agriculture and forestry.
- **Objective 1.2.2:** Improve practices for adaptation and mitigation of climate change in agriculture and forestry.
- **Objective 1.2.3:** Increase access to climate information, early warning systems, and climate-resilient technologies.

### Activities

- **Activity 1.2.1:** Develop and disseminate knowledge products on climate-smart agriculture and forestry.
- **Activity 1.2.2:** Provide training and capacity building for farmers and foresters on climate-smart practices.
- **Activity 1.2.3:** Establish and strengthen climate information services.

### Outputs

- **Output 1.2.1:** Knowledge products developed and disseminated.
- **Output 1.2.2:** Farmers and foresters trained in climate-smart practices.
- **Output 1.2.3:** Climate information services established and strengthened.

## Chapter 1.3: Reduce Emissions from Deforestation and Forest Degradation (REDD+)

### Objective

Reduce emissions from deforestation and forest degradation, enhance forest carbon stocks, and support sustainable management of forests and enhancement of forest carbon stocks.

### Key Results

- **Objective 1.3.1:** Reduce emissions from deforestation.
- **Objective 1.3.2:** Enhance forest carbon stocks.
- **Objective 1.3.3:** Support sustainable management of forests.

### Activities

- **Activity 1.3.1:** Develop and implement policies for reducing deforestation.
- **Activity 1.3.2:** Implement activities to enhance forest carbon stocks.
- **Activity 1.3.3:** Promote sustainable forest management practices.

### Outputs

- **Output 1.3.1:** Policies developed and implemented.
- **Output 1.3.2:** Activities implemented to enhance forest carbon stocks.
- **Output 1.3.3:** Sustainable forest management practices promoted.

## Chapter 1.4: Enhance Exchanges from Best-Practicing Countries and Experts (IEFA, UCN, ENABEL)

### Objective

Enhance exchanges of knowledge and best practices among countries to improve climate-smart agriculture and forestry practices.

### Key Results

- **Objective 1.4.1:** Knowledge exchanged among countries.
- **Objective 1.4.2:** Best practices adopted from other countries.
- **Objective 1.4.3:** Capacity built for knowledge exchange.

### Activities

- **Activity 1.4.1:** Organize exchanges of experts and best-practice visits.
- **Activity 1.4.2:** Develop and disseminate case studies on successful practices.
- **Activity 1.4.3:** Provide training on knowledge exchange methodologies.

### Outputs

- **Output 1.4.1:** Exchanges of experts organized.
- **Output 1.4.2:** Case studies developed and disseminated.
- **Output 1.4.3:** Training provided on knowledge exchange methodologies.

Along with the three EES (EEMAEL and SUMED), the NSC will include the SPMU (SPM Project Management Unit) to ensure effective implementation of the project. The Ministry of Environment (MoE) will be responsible for the overall management of the project, including national level coordination of CSOs, and relevant other organizations, as needed.

## Project Management Unit

The Project Management Unit (PMU), established under the PA, is a system designed to help ensure that projects are implemented efficiently. The PMU will be managed by the MoE in a Family Reunification Approach. The PMU will be responsible for the overall management of the project and will provide technical assistance to the EE and CSOs. The PMU will also be provided with a Ministry of Environment to coordinate the activities of the project.

### The Project

The project document, or Project Proposal, is the basic document that describes the project. It includes the objectives, scope, and implementation plan for the project. The project proposal is prepared by the EE and CSOs and is approved by the NCB.

The project will use GCF and management guidelines to "take into account" the needs of the PMU and sub-national organizations. The project will be implemented in accordance with the GCF's Environmental and Social Safeguards (ESS) and Gender Policy, as well as the MoE's ESS and Gender Policy.

### Project Components

The project will include the following components:

1. **Component 1: EE Capacity Building**

Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) including Youth, Women, and Children are key stakeholders in the project. They will be involved in all stages of the project from planning to implementation and monitoring. The CSOs will also be represented on the EE Board to ensure their voices are heard and their concerns addressed.

### Gender Equality

The project will promote gender equality by ensuring that women and men have equal access to resources, opportunities, and decision-making processes. The project will also address any gender-specific needs and vulnerabilities.

# Green Climate Fund Funding Proposal

## B

### Public Expenditure and Institutional Capacity

The key to implementing and scaling up the transformational change needed to address climate change is the development of the institutional capacity of countries to manage resources effectively and efficiently. This requires a strong focus on public expenditure management, including budgeting, procurement, accounting, auditing, monitoring, and evaluation. It also involves strengthening the capacity of institutions to implement policies and programs that support sustainable development.

### Climate-Smart Agriculture

Agriculture is one of the most vulnerable sectors to climate change and food insecurity. Climate-smart agriculture can help farmers adapt to changing climatic conditions and improve their productivity and resilience. This includes practices such as conservation agriculture, agroforestry, and integrated pest management. It also involves improving access to weather information and early warning systems.

### Land Tenure and Property Rights

Secure land tenure is essential for sustainable development. It provides the basis for investment in long-term improvements to agricultural lands and promotes efficient use of resources. It also helps to reduce conflict over land and natural resources, which can be exacerbated by climate change.

### Climate Finance

Climate finance refers to financial resources provided to support climate-related activities. This includes investments in mitigation and adaptation projects as well as policy and institutional reforms. The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is a key source of climate finance for developing countries.

### Energy Efficiency

Energy efficiency is a critical component of sustainable development. It involves the use of energy more efficiently, reducing waste and improving productivity. This can be achieved through a range of measures, including the adoption of energy-efficient technologies, improvements in building design, and changes in behavior.

### Renewable Energy

Renewable energy is an important part of the transition to a low-carbon economy. It includes sources such as solar, wind, hydro, and geothermal power. The use of renewable energy can help to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improve energy security.

### Water Management

Water management is essential for sustainable development. It involves the efficient use of water resources and the protection of ecosystems. This can be achieved through a range of measures, including improvements in irrigation systems, the promotion of water-efficient crops, and the protection of wetlands and other ecosystems.

### Disaster Risk Reduction

Disaster risk reduction is an important part of climate change adaptation. It involves the identification and management of risks associated with natural hazards such as floods, droughts, and storms. This can be achieved through a range of measures, including early warning systems, improvements in infrastructure, and the promotion of community-based disaster risk management.

### Health

Climate change has significant impacts on health. It can lead to increased incidence of diseases such as malaria and dengue fever, as well as heat-related illnesses. It also affects food security and water quality, which can have indirect effects on health. Addressing these challenges requires a multi-sectoral approach that involves the health sector as well as other sectors.

### Education

Education is an important part of sustainable development. It helps to raise awareness of climate change and its impacts, as well as the need for action. It also provides the skills and knowledge needed to implement climate change solutions. This includes education on renewable energy, energy efficiency, and climate-smart agriculture.

Stakeholders will need this dissemination effort to ensure sustainability at national level and emphasize learning and capacity building for future climate change financing. The project will ensure that MFIs have relevant financing mechanisms in place, and that they are able to provide loans to smallholder farmers and other vulnerable groups through climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices. This will enhance the resilience of farming communities and help sustainable development.

### General Objectives

The project's objectives will directly enhance the climate resilience of farming communities and help sustainable development. The project will ensure that MFIs have relevant financing mechanisms in place, and that they are able to provide loans to smallholder farmers and other vulnerable groups through climate-smart agriculture (CSA) practices. This will enhance the resilience of farming communities and help sustainable development.

The project will also enhance the capacity of MFIs to manage climate risks and opportunities by providing them with relevant knowledge and tools, such as climate information services, early warning systems, and risk management strategies. The project will also support the development of CSA practices among smallholder farmers and other vulnerable groups, which are the main suppliers of the value chains in the EP.

### Specific Objectives

1. **Objective 1:** Enhance the capacity of MFIs to manage climate risks and opportunities by providing them with relevant knowledge and tools.
2. **Objective 2:** Support the development of CSA practices among smallholder farmers and other vulnerable groups, which are the main suppliers of the value chains in the EP.

### Implementation Strategy

The project will be implemented through a combination of training, capacity building, and technical assistance. The project will also work closely with relevant stakeholders, such as government agencies, non-governmental organizations (NGOs), civil society organizations (CSOs), and other development partners to ensure sustainability and effectiveness.

The project will also use innovative approaches, such as mobile technology and digital platforms, to enhance the reach and impact of the project. The project will also promote gender equality and social inclusion by ensuring that women and marginalized groups are included in the project activities.

## ENVIRONMENT AGENCY

### ENVIRONMENT FOR LONG-TERM AND SUSTAINABLE IMPLEMENTATION PROJECT RESULTS AND BENEFITS

The project aims to address the need for long-term and sustainable implementation of project results and benefits. It will also promote the development of national capacities in climate change mitigation, adaptation, and technology transfer. The project will support the development of national strategies and policies on climate change, including the integration of climate change into national development plans and programs.

#### Objectives

- **Objective 1:** Strengthen institutional arrangements at country and district levels to enhance capacities for funding mobilization, planning, and implementation of climate change adaptation projects.
- **Objective 2:** Enhance regional networks of technical expertise to support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure and sustainable land management practices.
- **Objective 3:** Promote the development of national strategies and policies on climate change mitigation, adaptation, and technology transfer.

#### Activities

- **Activity 1.1:** Establish a national climate change fund to provide long-term financing for climate change projects.
- **Activity 1.2:** Develop and implement a national climate change strategy that includes measures to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and enhance resilience to the impacts of climate change.
- **Activity 1.3:** Strengthen regional networks of technical expertise to support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure and sustainable land management practices.

#### Outputs

- **Output 1.1:** A national climate change fund established with initial capitalization from domestic sources.
- **Output 1.2:** A national climate change strategy developed and approved by the government.
- **Output 1.3:** Regional networks of technical expertise established to support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure and sustainable land management practices.

#### Indicators

- **Indicator 1.1:** Number of projects funded through the national climate change fund.
- **Indicator 1.2:** Percentage of greenhouse gas emissions reduced compared to business-as-usual scenarios.
- **Indicator 1.3:** Number of regional networks established to support the development of climate-resilient infrastructure and sustainable land management practices.

#### Monitoring and Evaluation

The project will be monitored and evaluated using a results-based approach. Indicators will be developed for each output, and data will be collected regularly to track progress towards achieving the project's objectives.

## D1 Impact promoted (net, SRM weighted) 1 page

The project promotes a range of environmental and social benefits. - Improved air quality
- Reduced water usage
- Increased biodiversity

These benefits are achieved through the project's activities which include:

- Planting trees
- Installing renewable energy systems
- Improving soil health

The project promotes gender equality measures to address the disproportionate number of women in agriculture and domestic work. It also supports local economic development by creating jobs and stimulating local business.

## D2 GHG emissions avoided 1 page

The project will avoid greenhouse gas emissions through the following activities:

- Planting trees
- Installing renewable energy systems
- Improving soil health

These activities will avoid emissions of approximately 50,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent per year. This is achieved by:

- Increasing carbon sequestration in forests
- Reducing fossil fuel use for electricity and heating
- Improving agricultural practices to reduce methane and nitrous oxide emissions

## D3 Additional benefits 1 page

The project will deliver additional benefits beyond the primary environmental and social objectives. These include:

- Improved water quality
- Increased biodiversity
- Enhanced community resilience

These benefits are achieved through activities such as:

- Planting trees which improve soil health and water retention
- Installing renewable energy systems which reduce air pollution
- Improving agricultural practices which enhance soil fertility and reduce erosion

- PS2: Indigenous Peoples

## Purpose of the allocation and outcome statement targets for the "Renewable NDC" National Strategy for Climate Change

### Short: 1-3 years; medium: (3-5 years) and long-term (5+ years) as needed; changes, during or after project completion.

Green Climate Fund (GCF) resources will be allocated to support and validate measures to accelerate the transition towards a low-carbon economy. The proposed interventions aim to promote renewable energy, improve energy efficiency, and enhance climate resilience. This includes supporting the development of renewable energy projects, improving access to clean energy technologies, and implementing climate change adaptation strategies.

Component 1: This component will finance the highly degraded land through the project's efforts. While promoting the project's efforts to conserve biodiversity in the long term, it focuses on sustainable land management practices. The project will support the development of sustainable land management practices that improve soil health, increase carbon sequestration, and enhance ecosystem services.

Component 2: This component will finance the development of renewable energy projects. It aims to promote the use of renewable energy technologies such as solar, wind, and hydro power. The project will also support the development of energy efficiency measures in buildings and industries. The project will provide technical assistance to help communities adopt these technologies and improve their access to clean energy.

Component 3: This component will finance the development of climate-resilient infrastructure. It aims to promote the construction of climate-resilient infrastructure such as flood protection, drainage systems, and early warning systems. The project will also support the development of climate-resilient agriculture practices that help farmers adapt to changing weather patterns.

The project will be implemented over a period of 10 years. The first phase of the project will focus on the development of renewable energy projects. The second phase will focus on the promotion of energy efficiency measures in buildings and industries. The third phase will focus on the development of climate-resilient infrastructure. The fourth phase will focus on the promotion of climate-resilient agriculture practices.

The project will be implemented by a consortium of international and national organizations with expertise in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and climate change adaptation. The project will be coordinated by the Ministry of Environment and Natural Resources.

Farmers and PMFCs will also be involved to support local products and services (Output 3). Component 1 aims to promote sustainable land management practices that improve soil health, increase carbon sequestration, and enhance ecosystem services. Component 2 aims to promote the development of renewable energy projects that provide clean energy to communities.

The project will be implemented in collaboration with local governments, civil society organizations, and other stakeholders. The project will also involve the private sector to promote public-private partnerships for climate change adaptation and mitigation.

The project will be monitored and evaluated using a results-based framework. The project will also be subject to an independent evaluation to ensure that it is achieving its objectives.

#### 3.1 Needs of the rural communities

The rural communities have a population density of 470 per km² and an annual population growth rate of 2.5%. Needs is one of the new districts in the Eastern Region with a population of about 80,000 people. The district has a total land area of 169 sq. km. The district is located between latitude 7° 30' N and longitude 0° 25' W.

In the rural areas, there are no properly structured schools as they usually operate from rented buildings or private homes with poor facilities. There are also no health centers in the area. The communities lack access to clean water and electricity. The communities have no proper roads for transportation of goods and services. The communities lack access to financial institutions.

#### 3.2 Need for strengthening institutions and implementation capacity

The establishment of planning and coordination mechanisms is fundamental to ensure that the proposed project is implemented effectively. This requires the development of a strong institutional framework, including the following:

- **Capacity building:** Training and capacity building programs should be developed to enhance the skills and knowledge of local government officials, community leaders, and other stakeholders.
- **Coordination:** A coordination mechanism should be established to ensure effective collaboration between different actors involved in the project implementation.
- **Monitoring and evaluation:** A monitoring and evaluation system should be put in place to track progress and ensure that the project is on track to achieve its objectives.

The project will also require strong political support from local government officials, community leaders, and other stakeholders. This support is essential for ensuring that the project is implemented effectively and that it has a lasting impact on the communities it serves.

The natural Trustee Service Strategy Plan proposed a five-year plan and program budget of about USD 65 million for the period July 2018 to June 2023. The study was conducted to determine the feasibility of implementing the Green Climate Fund (GCF) Readiness and Implementation Support (RIS) program in the Philippines.

The RIS program aims to support the country's climate change adaptation and mitigation efforts by providing technical assistance, capacity building, and financial resources. The program will be implemented over a five-year period from 2018 to 2023, with an annual budget of USD 65 million.

### Objectives

- To enhance the capacity of the Philippines to access GCF funds.
- To support the implementation of climate change adaptation and mitigation projects in the country.
- To build the capacity of local institutions to manage and implement climate change projects.
- To promote the development of a green economy in the Philippines.

### Scope of Work

The scope of work for the RIS program includes:

- Technical assistance to support the development of climate change projects.
- Capacity building for local institutions to manage and implement climate change projects.
- Financial resources to support the implementation of climate change projects.
- Monitoring and evaluation of the impact of the RIS program.

### Methodology

The methodology for the feasibility study included a review of relevant literature, stakeholder consultations, and an analysis of the current climate change landscape in the Philippines. The study also considered the experiences of other countries that have implemented similar programs.

### Findings

The findings of the feasibility study indicated that the RIS program is feasible and could be successfully implemented in the Philippines. The study also identified several challenges that would need to be addressed, including:

- The need for strong political will and leadership.
- The need for adequate funding.
- The need for capacity building and technical assistance.
- The need for effective monitoring and evaluation.

### Recommendations

Based on the findings of the feasibility study, the following recommendations were made:

- The government should provide strong political will and leadership to support the implementation of the RIS program.
- The government should allocate adequate funding for the RIS program.
- Local institutions should be provided with capacity building and technical assistance to manage and implement climate change projects.
- Effective monitoring and evaluation systems should be put in place to track the impact of the RIS program.

### Conclusion

The feasibility study concluded that the RIS program is feasible and could be successfully implemented in the Philippines. The study also highlighted the need for strong political will, adequate funding, capacity building, and effective monitoring and evaluation to ensure the success of the program.

## Agriculture Policy is a vision of farming a productive, green and mixed-use agriculture sector.

The Green Climate Fund (GCF) is a unique financing instrument which supports mitigation and adaptation projects and programmes in developing countries. The GCF was established within the framework of the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC) in 2010 as an operating entity of the Financial Mechanism to assist developing countries party to the Convention. The GCF serves to promote a paradigm shift towards low-emission and climate-resilient development, taking into account the needs of nations that are particularly vulnerable to the adverse impacts of climate change.

### Government agencies used as Baseline Framework Authority (BFA)

- **Baseline Natural Resource Authority (BNRA)**
- **Baseline Ministry of Agriculture**
- **Baseline Ministry of Environment**
- **Baseline Ministry of Finance**

The GCF funding proposal is based on the following documents:

1. **Natural Resources Management Plan 2015-2025** (NRMP) and National Forest Management Plan 2017-2037, which reflect an overall strategy for sustainable management of natural resources.
2. **Baseline Framework Document** (BFD), which provides a baseline against which the impacts of GCF-funded projects will be measured.

### Existing GCF country programmes

The current GCF country programme is based on the management and protection of natural forests, biodiversity conservation, and climate change adaptation. The programme aims to:

- **Conserve biodiversity** by protecting critical habitats.
- **Promote sustainable forest management**.
- **Enhance community resilience** through improved livelihoods.

### Project objectives

The project aims to achieve the following specific objectives:

1. **Reduce greenhouse gas emissions** from deforestation and forest degradation.
2. **Improve forest governance** and enhance local communities' participation in forest management.
3. **Strengthen national capacities** for climate change adaptation and mitigation.

### Project components

The project will be implemented through the following components:

- **Component 1: Forest Conservation**
  - Protect critical habitats and reduce deforestation rates.
  - Enhance law enforcement and community engagement.

- **Component 2: Sustainable Forest Management**
  - Promote sustainable forest management practices.
  - Improve forest inventory and monitoring systems.

- **Component 3: Capacity Building**
  - Strengthen national capacities for climate change adaptation and mitigation.
  - Provide training and technical assistance to local communities.

### Project outcomes

The project is expected to achieve the following outcomes:

1. **Reduced greenhouse gas emissions** from deforestation and forest degradation.
2. **Improved forest governance** and enhanced community participation in forest management.
3. **Enhanced national capacities** for climate change adaptation and mitigation.

### Project implementation

The project will be implemented over a period of 10 years, with the following key milestones:

- **Year 1-3: Preparation and Planning**
  - Develop detailed project plans and budgets.
  - Establish partnerships and stakeholder engagement.

- **Year 4-7: Implementation**
  - Implement forest conservation activities.
  - Promote sustainable forest management practices.

- **Year 8-10: Monitoring, Evaluation, and Reporting**
  - Monitor and evaluate project progress.
  - Report on project outcomes and impacts.

The GCF granted a loan to South Africa for the financial equivalent of R1 billion (around R1.1 billion) from its Green Climate Fund (GCF) resources and co-financing from the Government of South Africa (GoSA). The project is part of the GCF’s support to South Africa’s Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs), which are the country’s commitments under the Paris Agreement. The project aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 34% below business-as-usual levels by 2025 and 42% by 2030, compared with a baseline of 2010.

The project will support South Africa in achieving its NDCs through the following activities:

- **Renewable Energy**: Support for renewable energy projects to increase the share of renewable energy in the electricity mix.
- **Energy Efficiency**: Improving energy efficiency in buildings and industries, including support for energy-efficient appliances and lighting.
- **Sustainable Transport**: Promoting sustainable transport systems, such as electric vehicles and public transportation.

The project will also support capacity building and technical assistance to enhance South Africa’s ability to implement climate change mitigation measures. The project is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 34% below business-as-usual levels by 2025 and 42% by 2030, compared with a baseline of 2010.

The GCF grant will support the Government of South Africa’s efforts to achieve its NDCs. The project is part of the GCF’s broader portfolio of climate finance activities in South Africa, which aims to support the country’s transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.

The project will be implemented by the Department of Environmental Affairs (DEA) and the Development Bank of Southern Africa (DBSA). The DEA is responsible for coordinating and implementing climate change policies and programs in South Africa. The DBSA is a development finance institution that provides financing and support for infrastructure projects in South Africa.

The project will be implemented over a period of five years, from 2017 to 2022. The total cost of the project is estimated at R1.1 billion, with the GCF providing a grant of R1 billion and the GoSA providing co-financing of R100 million.

The project will support South Africa’s efforts to achieve its NDCs by promoting renewable energy, improving energy efficiency, and supporting sustainable transport systems. The project is expected to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 34% below business-as-usual levels by 2025 and 42% by 2030, compared with a baseline of 2010.

The GCF grant will support the Government of South Africa’s efforts to achieve its NDCs. The project is part of the GCF’s broader portfolio of climate finance activities in South Africa, which aims to support the country’s transition to a low-carbon and climate-resilient economy.

A second major feature of the risk mitigation proposal is that funds will be provided by international financial institutions with experience for agriculture as part of their investment portfolios. Long-term finance will be contracted through commercial banks and other financial intermediaries. Additions to capital are expected to include grants, USD 10M of funds by local governments, and USD 5M from the private sector. The remaining amount will be covered by project implementation. It has been shown that this budget is feasible.

Green bond income estimates being used for farmers in the Eastern Province include costs of irrigating farms in farming communities, leasing land, the building of dams, and other infrastructure. These costs are estimated at USD 10M per year. The Green Climate Fund (GCF) and other groups will be approached to provide additional funding.

For the 10,000 hectares of rice fields that will be converted by project operators during 1-2 years, an estimated USD 500,000 is needed for management costs, equipment for 700 of the very smallholders and which are sharing resources before being able to start.

The scenario assumes that the operator is supported with THPFA support and the remaining BAU has been reduced gradually over time. NPV in the project period is USD 1,075,894. ### Table 1: Summary of the net cash flows for the different scenarios

| Scenario | Year 1 | Year 5 | Year 10 | Year 20 |
|----------|--------|--------|---------|---------|
| **BAU** - Business as Usual | 38.96 | 114.73 | 166.44 | 199.53 |
| **BAU** - 10% reduced with TREPA support | 29.83 | 104.45 | 157.16 | 191.36 |
| **BAU** - 20% reduced with TREPA support | 20.70 | 95.18 | 147.89 | 182.10 |
| **BAU** - 30% reduced with TREPA support | 11.56 | 85.91 | 138.62 | 172.83 |

### Note

Note that the best restoration option detailed (Option 1) generates large and positive net cash flows and enhances biodiversity, employing sustainable forest management practices. The option also reduces greenhouse gas emissions by 40% compared to BAU. The option is based on a combination of:

1. Improved timber sales from the additional 20 years of rotation.
2. Reduced harvesting costs resulting in lower stumpage fees.
3. Reduced infrastructure costs resulting in lower maintenance and management costs.

These benefits, which are significant, are captured by the farmers who restore the forests and offset wood and are transferred to the financial closed benefit analysis.

The option also provides a positive cash flow from restoration activities, almost twice as much as BAU, and even more if the cost of carbon is included. For Option 1 (implementation), investments in a nursery facility would yield a net internal rate of return (IRR) over 20 years of approximately 35%. The option also generates positive cash flows for the State Forest Agency over the first 6-7 years, and then over 100 years.

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.0 | PAGE 88 OF 119

**SUBMITTER:** Enabel and ICAMF will distribute a series of climate-resilient agriculture packages, including training materials and equipment to smallholder farmers in the Eastern Province. ROAM, village savings and loan associations (VSLAs), and farmer cooperatives will be trained on climate-smart agriculture techniques.

The following is a list of some of the key technologies and methodologies to be introduced:

- Tree fodder, grasses and herbaceous leguminous production for improving soil productivity.
- Business incorporation from fertilizer use for improving soil fertility.
- Improved water harvesting and storage systems for increasing business production.
- Improved agricultural systems e.g. pollarding and innovative fodder conservation for increased water supply through soil harvesting and bodies which detain ground water.

Other activities include:

- Clean and efficient cooking technologies.
- Climate-smart agriculture value chains, and
- Cross-sectoral planning and community landscape restoration planning.

## 1.1.5 Eligibility criteria for funding of activities under the GCF

In the absence of a clear legal framework, the eligibility of activities and expenditures is determined by the following criteria:

- The activity must be consistent with the objectives of the GCF.
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the UN Framework Convention on Climate Change (UNFCCC).
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the Paris Agreement.
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the Kyoto Protocol.
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the Cancun Agreements.
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the Durban Platform for Enhanced Action (DPA).
- The activity must be consistent with the principles of the Warsaw International Mechanism for Loss and Damage associated with Climate Change Impacts (WIM).

# GREEN CLIMATE FUND FUNDING PROPOSAL V2.0 | PAGE #1 OF 119

## D

### 1.1 Purpose and scope

All women and girls will gain to:

- Reduce their vulnerability to climate change impacts.
- Enhance their resilience to climate change impacts.

Particular attention should be given to the needs of:

- Women in rural areas.
- Indigenous peoples.
- Disabled persons.
- Older persons.
- Youth.

### 1.2 Eligibility criteria

Eligible projects must meet the following criteria:

- Be implemented by a national or local government agency, a non-governmental organization (NGO), or a community-based organization (CBO).
- Be designed to address climate change impacts and enhance resilience.
- Be consistent with the objectives of the Green Climate Fund (GCF) and the country's nationally determined contributions (NDCs).

### 1.3 Eligible activities

Eligible activities include, but are not limited to:

- Climate change mitigation projects that reduce greenhouse gas emissions from agriculture, forestry, and other land use.
- Climate change adaptation projects that enhance resilience to climate change impacts in rural areas.

### 1.4 Exclusion criteria

The following activities are excluded from eligibility:

- Projects that do not meet the eligibility criteria outlined above.
- Projects that are not consistent with the objectives of the GCF or the country's NDCs.

### 1.5 Monitoring, evaluation and reporting

All projects must include a monitoring, evaluation, and reporting component to ensure that they are achieving their intended outcomes and impacts.

### 1.6 Applicability

This proposal applies to all funding requests submitted under this call for proposals.

### 1.7 Submission of applications

Applications will be accepted in English or French only.

### 1.8 Timeline and process

The timeline and process for submitting applications is as follows:

- Call for proposals opens: [Date]
- Deadline for submission of concept notes: [Date]
- Review of concept notes: [Date]
- Invitation to submit full proposals: [Date]
- Deadline for submission of full proposals: [Date]
- Review of full proposals: [Date]
- Approval of funding: [Date]

### 1.9 Monitoring and evaluation

All projects must include a monitoring and evaluation component to ensure that they are achieving their intended outcomes and impacts.

### 1.10 Outputs and impact

The expected outputs and impacts of this proposal are as follows:

- Increased resilience of women and girls to climate change impacts.
- Reduced vulnerability of women and girls to climate change impacts.
- Enhanced capacity of national and local government agencies, NGOs, and CBOs to implement projects that address climate change impacts.

### 1.11 Risk management

All projects must include a risk management component to ensure that they are able to adapt to changing circumstances and maintain their intended outcomes and impacts.

### 1.12 Gender equality

This proposal is designed to promote gender equality and empower women and girls.

### 1.13 Safeguards

This proposal includes safeguards to protect the rights of indigenous peoples, local communities, and other vulnerable groups.

2. Identify the CDM projects that can be converted to CCS projects and provide technical assistance for conversion.

## Services to protect and restore ecosystems

### 3.4.1 Report on activities undertaken to implement the project

The project has been successfully implemented in accordance with the approved work plan. Key achievements include:

- Restoration of 50 hectares of degraded forest land.
- Planting of over 2,000 native tree species.
- Establishment of three community-based nurseries.

### 3.4.2 High-level description of activities undertaken

The project involved several key activities:

1. **Preparation and planning**: Conducted feasibility studies and developed a detailed work plan.
2. **Community engagement**: Mobilized local communities to participate in the restoration efforts.
3. **Nursery establishment**: Set up three community-based nurseries to grow native tree species.
4. **Planting and monitoring**: Planted over 2,000 trees and conducted regular monitoring to ensure survival rates.

### 3.4.3 Financial report

The financial report for the project is as follows:

- **Total budget**: $50,000
- **Actual expenditure**: $48,000
- **Remaining balance**: $2,000

### 3.4.4 Lessons learned and best practices

Key lessons learned from the implementation of the project include:

- **Community involvement**: Engaging local communities is crucial for the success of restoration projects.
- **Nursery management**: Establishing community-based nurseries ensures a steady supply of native tree species.
- **Monitoring and evaluation**: Regular monitoring helps to identify issues early and improve survival rates.

### 3.4.5 Future plans

Future plans include:

- Expanding the project to additional degraded areas.
- Increasing the number of community-based nurseries.
- Continuing regular monitoring and evaluation.

## Output 3.4 Emissions from best practices generated and abated:

### 3.4.1 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** NOx control in cement kilns
- **Description:** Cement kilns are a significant source of NOx emissions.
- **Emissions:** 50 kg CO2e per tonne of clinker produced.

### 3.4.2 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** NOx control in cement kilns
- **Mitigation:** Implementation of advanced combustion technologies and selective non-catalytic reduction (SNCR) systems.
- **Emissions Reduction:** 30 kg CO2e per tonne of clinker produced.

### 3.4.3 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Methane recovery from landfills
- **Description:** Landfills are a significant source of methane emissions.
- **Emissions:** 150 kg CO2e per tonne of waste disposed.

### 3.4.4 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Methane recovery from landfills
- **Mitigation:** Installation of gas collection and utilization systems to capture and burn methane.
- **Emissions Reduction:** 100 kg CO2e per tonne of waste disposed.

### 3.4.5 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** HFC refrigerants in supermarkets
- **Description:** Supermarkets use HFCs as refrigerants, which have high global warming potential.
- **Emissions:** 100 kg CO2e per tonne of refrigerant used.

### 3.4.6 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** HFC refrigerants in supermarkets
- **Mitigation:** Transition to natural refrigerants such as ammonia or carbon dioxide.
- **Emissions Reduction:** 80 kg CO2e per tonne of refrigerant used.

### 3.4.7 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Deforestation for agriculture
- **Description:** Deforestation is a significant source of CO2 emissions.
- **Emissions:** 500 kg CO2e per hectare deforested.

### 3.4.8 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Deforestation for agriculture
- **Mitigation:** Implementation of agroforestry practices and sustainable farming methods.
- **Emissions Reduction:** 300 kg CO2e per hectare preserved.

### 3.4.9 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Coal-fired power plants
- **Description:** Coal-fired power plants are a significant source of CO2 emissions.
- **Emissions:** 1000 kg CO2e per MWh generated.

### 3.4.10 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Coal-fired power plants
- **Mitigation:** Implementation of carbon capture and storage (CCS) technologies.
- **Emissions Reduction:** 500 kg CO2e per MWh generated.

## Output 3.5 Emissions from worst practices avoided:

### 3.5.1 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Open-pit mining
- **Description:** Open-pit mining releases significant amounts of methane and other greenhouse gases.
- **Emissions:** 200 kg CO2e per tonne of ore extracted.

### 3.5.2 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Open-pit mining
- **Mitigation:** Transition to underground mining methods to reduce emissions.
- **Emissions Avoidance:** 150 kg CO2e per tonne of ore extracted.

### 3.5.3 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Diesel-powered vehicles
- **Description:** Diesel-powered vehicles emit significant amounts of NOx and particulate matter.
- **Emissions:** 150 kg CO2e per tonne-kilometer traveled.

### 3.5.4 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Diesel-powered vehicles
- **Mitigation:** Transition to electric or hybrid vehicles to reduce emissions.
- **Emissions Avoidance:** 100 kg CO2e per tonne-kilometer traveled.

### 3.5.5 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Chemical manufacturing
- **Description:** Chemical manufacturing processes release significant amounts of greenhouse gases.
- **Emissions:** 300 kg CO2e per tonne of product manufactured.

### 3.5.6 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Chemical manufacturing
- **Mitigation:** Implementation of energy-efficient processes and waste reduction strategies.
- **Emissions Avoidance:** 150 kg CO2e per tonne of product manufactured.

### 3.5.7 Practice Emissions:
- **Practice:** Coal-fired heating systems
- **Description:** Coal-fired heating systems emit significant amounts of CO2 and other pollutants.
- **Emissions:** 200 kg CO2e per MWh generated.

### 3.5.8 Practice Mitigations:
- **Practice:** Coal-fired heating systems
- **Mitigation:** Transition to renewable energy sources such as solar or wind power.
- **Emissions Avoidance:** 150 kg CO2e per MWh generated.

### 3.5.9 Practice Emissions:

- **Description:** Oil and gas flaring releases significant amounts of methane and other greenhouse gases.
